name: TimeComponentClientFacet_SyncDayPhase
summary: The time facet's day-phase sync. 12-byte record: the shared two-u64 head then one u32 BE holding the value 2 in the one captured instance. The writer FUN_1426d64f0 emits exactly head + one u32 and nothing else, and the reader FUN_1426d6530 consumes the same two fields, which is what accounts for 16+4 = 20 body bytes against the 24-byte record.
purpose: Tell the client which day phase it is in. The captured value 2 is the only phase ever seen, so the enum's members are not enumerated; what phase 0 or 1 mean is unmeasured. The value is carried as a plain u32 rather than an enum because the closed vocabulary has no named enum for it and only one member is observed.

created_when: the server changes the time facet's day phase
lifecycle.if_absent: the client's day phase never changes. The lab measured that traffic of this kind refreshes the client's InGame activity clock, so a stream that stops is followed by the client's own timeout watchdog

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the wide prefix varint 97 42, i.e. type index 4247 = 0x1097. fields[] below use BODY offsets, so the first body byte is at 0x00 and the 24-byte record starts 4 bytes earlier.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured 93 a3 e4 77 cb 5f d5 1e = 0x93a3e477cb5fd51e. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id, which here is the TimeComponentClientFacet. The SAME value appears in 0x1096, in the client's 0x1098 SyncToClient, and in the client's 0x1096/0x1097 request direction, which is the per-component proof: one component, one local id.
fields.provenance: msg.time-sync-to-client.json names it from the decompiled accessor FUN_1416c1c40 and the registration key FUN_14167c560; measured corpus-wide on 2026-11-09 across 36 R records of 10 types

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Measured bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a = 0xbf85314bbc4a951a. Second u64 of the shared head: the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id, written big-endian. Read little-endian those bytes are 1a954abc4b3185bf, the front half of the actor id ClientAddEntryMsg (0xa4) hands the client.
fields.provenance: already earned in msg.time-sync-to-client.json (writer FUN_1414dbca0 via htonl64 FUN_1461668a0); re-measured here

fields.name: day_phase
fields.note: Measured 00 00 00 02. The writer FUN_1426d64f0 copies object +0x20 through the generic u32 BE primitive FUN_140876e70 after the shared head, and the reader FUN_1426d6530 reads the same one u32 back; both stop there. The same primitive FUN_140876e70 is the one the atlas already pinned as 'writes u32 BE' for the Territory batch, so the codec is a second, independent confirmation and not a guess. Only the value 2 has ever been seen, so the phase names stay unnamed and the field is carried as u32be rather than a named enum.
fields.provenance: capture: 0x76_T0x1097_R.bin body[0x10..0x14]; decompile: writer FUN_1426d64f0 and reader FUN_1426d6530 on build 30fe6461

evidence.ref: object vtable 0x1482feed8, resolved by the name-accessor walk (its +0x08 slot is the name accessor: see the sentence that names the string). Message-object slots, using the convention meanings.md established on 2026-10-29 for 0xf37 and 0xda2, where the MARSHAL thunk 0x1414c0730 is `mov rax,[rdx]; jmp [rax+0x60]`: +0x58 = FUN_14406f4b0 is the APPLY handler, which resolves a manager singleton through FUN_1416bd7c0 and copies the value in without ever touching the stream; +0x60 = FUN_1426d64f0 is the WRITER, which serializes the body onto the stream; +0x68 = FUN_1426d6530 is the READER, which deserializes the body off the stream

writer FUN_1426d64f0 is exactly five instructions of work: FUN_1414dbca0() for the shared head, then load object +0x20 and pass it to FUN_140876e70. No other read. apply FUN_14406f4b0 mirrors it with FUN_14408d5f0. That fixes the body at 16 + 4 = 20 bytes
record 0x76_T0x1097_R.bin at seq 0x76, 24 bytes: 00 01 97 42 | 93a3e477cb5fd51e | bf85314bbc4a951a | 00000002. The captured body is 20 bytes, exactly head + one u32

the reader is the SAME function the atlas already recorded as the reader for 0xad4 TerritoryInteractorComponentServerFacet_RequestRoster ('head-only 16 B', writer 0x14259f170 / reader 0x14259f180) and 0xad3 RequestSignupCount. A shared codec slot across three unrelated messages is an independent signal that the layout is head + u32 and not something this record happens to fit
